evidence.claim: From 1913 to 1996, the village was home to the Flxible Company, which manufactured motorcycle sidecars, commercial cars and buses.
evidence.quote: From 1913 to 1996, Loudonville was home to The Flxible Company, a manufacturer of motorcycle sidecars, commercial cars (hearses, ambulances, and flower cars), intercity coaches, and city-transit coaches.

evidence.claim: During World War II, the company interrupted normal production to make war goods.
evidence.quote: During World War II, Flxible interrupted its normal production and instead built a variety of war goods.

evidence.claim: A portion of the former plant later served as a parts depot and service point for Motor Coach Industries until that operation ended in December 2014.
evidence.quote: A part of the former Flxible plant was in use as a parts depot and service point for Motor Coach Industries until December 5, 2014, when all production was shut down.
